output.summary: The yield drop is real: the gauge R&R is stable, the CMM program is unchanged and the tolerances are unchanged. The new operators are ruled out, because they perform no worse than experienced operators and yield fell before they ran alone. Three causes remain confounded in time. These are 12-hour shifts, the Corvane lots with wider hardness spread, and the deferred spindle service, with runout above limit on L3-02 and L3-05. The scrap-tag timestamps are batch-entry artefacts, so they say nothing about fatigue. The long-shaft tolerance also confounds the machine comparison. The Line 6 Corvane data, the hour-of-machining reconstruction and the staggered service trials would separate the causes. The deferral was driven by backlog pressure. Reverting shifts, cancelling Corvane, punishing operators or cutting inspection are unjustified or harmful. Running the staggered service and trial design is best.
